newsitem.title: UK: NEXT 10-12 DAYS CRUCIAL FOR S.ENGLAND WHEAT CROPS.
newsitem.headline: NEXT 10-12 DAYS CRUCIAL FOR S.ENGLAND WHEAT CROPS.

text.p: The next 10-12 days are crucial for wheat quality in southern England, farming sources said.
"That's when the quality will be made or lost," one said. "It's a worry."
Yields overall would probably not be too bad, he said. But with prices already low, farmers were concerned that too much rain would shift more wheat into the feed category.
The other problem with rain was that it delayed harvesting. More rain was forecast in the next couple of days, he said.

"It doesn't look too good," one Hampshire based agriculture source said of the wheat crop. The rain had not been accompanied by wind, so not too much had been knocked flat. But there were problems with fungus, triggered by the damp.
In his area there was still some time to go before the wheat harvest got underway, giving crops a chance to recover. Farmers on the coast in Sussex would be worse hit, he reckoned.
Worst hit area has been the south-west, where heavy rain has halted harvesting in most places, according to farming sources there.
"Torrential rain looks set to flatten any crops still standing," the regional National Farmers Union said in a statement.
Atrocious weather "could wipe off much of what limited value remains on wheat and barley by rendering it fit only for animal feed rather than bread or beer making," the south-west NFU said.
